agent_summary:
Lane API (WSTG-APIT-01, "Test GraphQL") — item marked DONE. Result: no GraphQL attack surface exists on juice.lab.test; it is a REST-only OWASP Juice Shop.

GraphQL testing (exhaustive, all negative): GET/POST /graphql and /graphiql, plus /subscriptions, /altair, /.well-known/apollo/server-health, and GET ?query= all return the Angular SPA index.html (200, no GraphQL processing); /api/graphql, /rest/graphql, /api/v1/graphql, /api/graphiql, /api/graphql/schema all return 500 "Unexpected path" from the Angular catch-all (angular.js). A real GraphQL introspection POST {"query":"{__schema...}"} to /graphql (approved write, x12) returned 200 index.html with no data/errors JSON. OPTIONS /graphql returned a generic CORS 204. The SPA main.js bundle (x8) references only REST endpoints and contains no GraphQL client code.

Additional API-surface coverage (depth floor): mapped the real REST API. Reachable without auth: /api/Products, /api/SecurityQuestions, /api/Feedbacks, /api/Recycles, /api/Quantitys, /api/Deliverys, /rest/products/search, /rest/products/{id}/reviews, /rest/admin/application-version, /rest/admin/application-configuration (23KB), /metrics, /rest/memories (leaks password hashes/tokens), /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub. Auth-required (401): /api/Users (collection), /api/Complaints, /api/Cards, /api/Addresss, /api/SecurityAnswers, /b2b/v2/orders. A Swagger/OpenAPI UI is served at /api-docs/ (swagger-ui-init.js embeds the spec). 

Confirmed (reproducing existing cross-lane leads) with test accounts apit1/apit2: BFLA on /api/Users collection (full user table + ?role=admin filter returned to a customer) and /api/BasketItems; BOLA on /api/Users/{id}, /api/BasketItems/{id}, /rest/basket/{id} (foreign baskets 1–6 readable, identical ETags across apit1/apit2). Correctly scoped: /rest/order-history/orders (403 admin-only), /api/Addresss and /api/Cards per-id (400), own order-history/wallet/addresses per account. 

New minor observation recorded as a lead: /api model routing is case-insensitive (/api/users, /api/USERS == /api/Users, same ETag), which can bypass case-sensitive path filters.

Nothing left open. All testing was read-only except one approved GraphQL introspection POST to /graphql against test account apit1. Display budget for response bodies was exhausted early; full bodies are retained as evidence for the auditor.

leads.title: [agent] No GraphQL API present on juice.lab.test (WSTG-APIT-01 negative result)

detail.text: GraphQL was tested across many vectors: GET/POST /graphql and /graphiql return the Angular SPA index.html (200, text/html) with no GraphQL processing; GET /api/graphql, /rest/graphql, /api/v1/graphql return HTTP 500 "Error: Unexpected path" from the Angular catch-all (angular.js); a GraphQL introspection POST {"query":"{__schema{queryType{name}}}"} to /graphql returned 200 serving index.html (no data/errors JSON); OPTIONS /graphql returned a generic CORS 204. The SPA main.js bundle references only REST endpoints (/api/* model routes, /rest/*) and contains no GraphQL client code. Conclusion: this OWASP Juice Shop instance exposes a REST API only, with no GraphQL attack surface.

leads.title: [agent] REST API routing is case-insensitive on /api model endpoints

detail.text: GET /api/users and /api/USERS return byte-identical responses (same ETag W/"2c7d-...") to GET /api/Users as customer apit1 — the full user table. Case-insensitive routing means any upstream protection keyed to the exact-case path (/api/Users) can be bypassed with a different case. Observed on juice.lab.test during API-lane testing.
